statement: The install task discovers which scripts to symlink onto PATH by globbing bin/sgt-* and bin/_sgt-*.sh rather than enumerating filenames, because a fixed enumeration silently drops newly added helpers.
trigger: operator runs the install task after cloning or updating the repo
outcome: every current and future sgt-* / _sgt-*.sh helper is linked onto PATH without the install task needing to be edited
notes: Old mechanism is a for-glob over bin/; the durable rule is discover-by-convention over enumerate-by-name.
rationale: A discovery convention reused by two tasks in the same file (install and uninstall both glob the same shape); it is deterministic machinery subordinate to the install checkpoint, not itself a checkpoint (ladder §6.5/§6.6).

statement: Uninstalling only removes a PATH symlink when its resolved target still points back inside this repository's bin/ directory, so an uninstall never deletes an unrelated file that happens to share a name.
trigger: operator runs the uninstall task
outcome: only symlinks this repo's install actually created are removed
rationale: Deterministic ownership-verification machinery subordinate to an uninstall checkpoint; not itself a durable outcome.

statement: Dependency checking distinguishes required tools, whose absence fails the check with a nonzero exit, from optional tools, whose absence only warns, so an operator can tell which gaps block use of Sergeant from which merely reduce functionality.
trigger: operator runs the dependency check task
outcome: the operator sees a pass/fail per dependency with an explicit required-vs-optional distinction and an install hint
notes: Direct precursor to sergeant-rs's own doctor/capability-report design (proposal §17.4).
rationale: A recognizable trigger (operator runs the check) and bounded outcome (pass/fail report) that can be invoked independently — matches §6.2's workflow test; the required/optional distinction is the durable outcome, not the printf mechanics.

statement: A dependency is verified as truly supported, not merely installed, by probing its help output for the exact flags the caller needs (--description, --json, --work-dir on td create --help) rather than trusting a version string alone.
trigger: the dependency check verifies the td task tracker
outcome: td is reported supported only when the exact flags Sergeant depends on are actually present in its help text
notes: Same capability-probe-via-help-output pattern as bin/_sgt-intent.sh's no-mistakes probe; a version number alone is not trusted as a capability proxy (L1-adjacent: measure the CLI, don't assume from a version).
rationale: Deterministic probing technique reused across two independent capability checks (td here, no-mistakes in _sgt-intent.sh) with the same contract: read the help text, don't infer from a version string.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap for a generic capability-probe primitive

statement: Detecting which interactive agent harness is available tries a fixed priority order of candidate executables (opencode, then goose, then claude) and reports only the first one found, rather than requiring the operator to pre-select one.
trigger: the dependency check looks for an interactive agent harness
outcome: the operator sees which harness Sergeant will use, chosen by priority order among installed candidates, without configuring anything
notes: Precedent for a prioritized Harness Registry lookup (proposal §17.1) rather than a single hardcoded harness name.
rationale: Deterministic detection machinery; the prioritized-list-of-candidates shape recurs at bin/_sgt-harness.sh's registry, so it is a reusable pattern rather than a one-off checkpoint.

statement: Skill discovery for the OpenCode harness is configured to look in two fixed roots: .agents/skills (the canonical cross-harness tree) and skills (repo-specific, ops-oriented skills).
trigger: OpenCode starts and needs to enumerate available skills
outcome: every skill under either root becomes discoverable to the OpenCode harness without per-skill registration
notes: Mirrors docs/repo-scoped-skills.md's convention (already P1); this is the machine-readable half of the same rule for one specific harness.
rationale: A reusable location convention consumed by every skill/workflow discovery path for this harness, not itself a bounded procedure.

statement: Before every git push, the drain test suite must run and pass; the push is blocked on failure unless the operator explicitly opts out with git push --no-verify.
trigger: operator runs git push
outcome: push proceeds only after the drain suite passes, or the operator explicitly consents to skipping validation
notes: Proposal §6.3 names 'release-verification' as its own illustrative example of a stage: 'If release-verification remains a meaningful boundary whether it is implemented by Bash, Python, GitHub Actions, or three commands, it is a stage.' This repo's own scripts/gate.sh + no-mistakes pipeline is the structural analogue.
rationale: Matches the ladder's own worked example verbatim: the checkpoint (validate before shipping) would survive being reimplemented by any mechanism; today's mechanism (git hook + mise + Docker) is incidental.

statement: If the tooling required to run the pre-push validation (mise, docker) is unavailable, the hook fails closed with exit 1 and an actionable message, rather than silently skipping validation and letting the push through.
trigger: required validation tooling is missing on push
outcome: a push with unrunnable validation is blocked with a diagnosis, never silently allowed through
notes: Direct precedent for CLAUDE.md's 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant applied to a shipping gate rather than to work-state recovery.
rationale: This is a judgment/fail-closed nuance attached to the release-verification checkpoint, not a separate checkpoint of its own (ladder §6.4).

statement: The pre-push hook locates the mise executable by trying a fixed priority order — the current PATH, then $HOME/.local/bin/mise, then $HOME/.cargo/bin/mise — rather than requiring it already be on PATH.
trigger: the pre-push hook needs to invoke mise
outcome: the hook still works from a git-hook environment where PATH may be minimal
rationale: Deterministic resolve-the-tool-location machinery subordinate to the release-verification checkpoint.

statement: Listing known projects treats the special file config.yaml under the Sergeant config directory as global configuration, not a project, and excludes it from the project listing.
trigger: operator runs sgt-list
outcome: the project list never shows a phantom 'config' project
rationale: A filtering rule needed only while listing; not itself a reusable procedure or a durable checkpoint.

statement: Listing projects is a bounded, independently invocable procedure: enumerate every project YAML under the Sergeant config directory (other than the reserved config.yaml) and print each with its optional description, failing with a diagnosis if the config directory or any project is absent.
trigger: operator wants to see which projects Sergeant knows about
outcome: a complete, human-readable enumeration of registered projects
rationale: Recognizable trigger and bounded, independently invocable outcome per §6.2.
alternatives_considered: stage of a broader project-management workflow

statement: Showing a project's status walks every configured repo and reports, per repo, whether it is cloned, its current branch, its working-tree cleanliness, and how far ahead/behind its upstream it is — never mutating anything.
trigger: operator wants a read-only snapshot of every repo in a project
outcome: a per-repo clone/branch/dirty/ahead-behind summary with no side effects
rationale: Bounded, side-effect-free, independently invocable outcome; matches §6.2.

statement: Syncing a project's repos treats three distinct repo states differently: an already-cloned repo on a named branch is pulled fast-forward-only (never merged), an existing non-git directory is left untouched with a warning, and a missing repo with a configured URL is cloned; every other combination is reported and skipped rather than guessed at.
trigger: operator runs sgt-sync <project>
outcome: every repo ends the run either cloned, pulled, or explicitly reported as needing manual attention — never silently skipped without a reason
rationale: Bounded, independently invocable procedure with a clear completion condition (every repo classified and acted on); matches §6.2.

statement: A repo pull only proceeds fast-forward and is skipped with a warning (never force-merged or rebased) when the branch has diverged or has no upstream, and a detached HEAD is skipped outright rather than guessed at.
trigger: an existing cloned repo is being synced
outcome: a repo is never mutated in a way the operator did not ask for; ambiguous local state is reported, not resolved automatically
rationale: A safety rule that applies while crossing the pull checkpoint; too narrow to be its own workflow, but broader than pure mechanics since it is a judgment about what NOT to do automatically.

statement: Removing a drain is explicitly idempotent: undraining a scope that is not currently drained still exits successfully, and --global and a named project are mutually exclusive scopes that cannot both be targeted in one invocation.
trigger: operator runs sgt-undrain for a project or --global
outcome: admission for the given scope is restored, or was already restored, with the same successful outcome either way
rationale: A meaningful durable checkpoint (admission restored) whose idempotency guarantee operators would care about regardless of implementation; matches §6.3.

statement: A DAG stage becoming ready triggers dispatch of a normal Sergeant work unit via the ordinary dispatch procedure, and the resulting fleet task is tagged with the external DAG's run and stage identifiers so a later polling pass can recognize which DAG stage that dispatched work belongs to.
trigger: an external DAG scheduler (dagr) reports one of its stages is ready to run
outcome: a normal dispatch happens and is durably tagged with which DAG run/stage it belongs to, so completion can be reported back
notes: dagr itself is an external tool this bin/ script defers to for ordering/dependency logic; Sergeant owns only the dispatch and the completion tagging.
rationale: The behavior — advance a multi-stage, dependency-ordered plan of dispatched work as stages complete — is exactly the branching/nested-workflow capability the proposal names as absent from the current engine (§7.7: 'True nested workflows do not exist yet'). Sergeant-rs delegates the whole capability to an external tool (dagr) rather than representing it; that delegation is itself the evidence a lower rung cannot cover this.
alternatives_considered: workflow (rejected: no bounded single-invocation outcome — the procedure spans an externally-scheduled multi-stage plan)

engine_gap.behavior: Advance a multi-stage plan of dispatched work units, where later stages become eligible only once their declared prerequisite stages complete, and completion of any stage must be durably attributable back to which plan/stage it satisfied.
engine_gap.evidence: sgt-dag-dispatch-hook and sgt-dag-run exist solely to bolt an external tool (dagr) onto sgt-dispatch/sgt-watch for exactly this purpose; every ordering, dependency, and advance-on-completion decision is made outside Sergeant.
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent the whole DAG as one ordinary workflow with several ordered stages (§6.2/§6.3)
Represent each DAG stage's dispatch as an actor stage invoking a shared helper (§6.5)
why_each_fails: A single workflow's stages run in one fixed, statically-authored sequence; a DAG's stages are dynamically gated on sibling completion across potentially many independently dispatched Works, which the current per-Work actor-stage engine has no way to express or observe.

A helper can dispatch one stage, but nothing in the engine owns 'which stages are now unblocked' as a durable fact recomputed from completion events — that ownership is exactly what dagr (external) supplies today.
engine_gap.minimum_capability_required: The runtime must be able to own a durable multi-Work dependency graph (or delegate to and observe an external one) and re-evaluate readiness from Work-completion events, advancing dependent Works without an external polling script.
engine_gap.acceptance_test: Given a project YAML with a dag: block declaring stage B after stage A, dispatching the DAG results in only A running; when A's Work reaches a terminal done state, B is dispatched automatically without any operator or external-tool action, and the dependency is checkable from durable state alone.

statement: A project's DAG is declared as data in the project YAML — named stages, each naming its repos, its td task or literal brief, and the stages it depends on (after:) — and sgt-dag-run reads that declaration to create/verify the DAG and start a run, rather than the DAG being written as imperative dispatch calls.
trigger: a project's work is expressed as a dependency-ordered multi-stage plan
outcome: the DAG's shape is legible as data in one place (the project YAML) rather than scattered across imperative dispatch invocations
notes: Directly parallel to proposal §4.4 'Procedure remains data' but applied to a capability class (branching/dependent multi-Work plans) the current sergeant-rs engine does not yet represent at all.
rationale: Same underlying capability gap as sgt-dag-dispatch-hook: an authored declarative dependency graph over dispatched Works, with no current engine concept to hold it.
alternatives_considered: shared-context (rejected: the declaration is meaningless without a runtime that acts on dependency edges, which does not exist)

engine_gap.behavior: Declare a named, dependency-ordered set of stages (each producing its own dispatched Work) as data, and have the runtime create/track that structure and start it, dispatching only the stages whose dependencies are already satisfied.
engine_gap.evidence: The dag: YAML block is pure declarative data (stage names, repos, td/brief source, after: dependency edges) that sgt-dag-run and sgt-dag-dispatch-hook interpret only by handing it to the external dagr tool.
lower_rungs_attempted: Store the dependency graph as ordinary shared context (§6.6) consulted by an actor stage
Represent it as one long workflow whose stages are statically ordered by declaration order
why_each_fails: Shared context can hold the data, but nothing reads and enforces it without a scheduler; today that scheduler is the external dagr binary, not Sergeant.
Static stage order cannot express fan-out/fan-in dependency shapes (e.g. two independent stages both gating a third) the after: field allows.
engine_gap.minimum_capability_required: A durable, engine-owned representation of a dependency graph over Works (or stages) plus the ability to react to a dependency's completion by admitting its dependents — i.e. the true nested/branching workflow capability the proposal already flags (§7.7) as future work.
engine_gap.acceptance_test: A project YAML dag: block with a fan-in dependency (two stages, both required by a third) results in the third stage's Work being dispatched only after both prerequisite Works reach a terminal done state, verifiable from durable engine state without consulting an external scheduler's own database.

statement: Initializing a treehouse worktree pool for a project's repos only acts on repos that are already cloned and skips (never fails) repos lacking a local clone, and it treats an already-present treehouse.toml as already-initialized rather than re-initializing.
trigger: operator runs sgt-treehouse-init for a project, optionally filtered by group
outcome: every eligible, not-yet-initialized, cloned repo gets a treehouse pool; nothing is skipped silently and nothing already initialized is redone
rationale: Bounded, independently invocable outcome (every eligible repo pooled) with an idempotence guarantee; matches §6.2/§6.3.
alternatives_considered: stage of a larger setup workflow

statement: Once repos have a treehouse pool initialized, dispatch automatically prefers a pre-warmed treehouse lease over a plain git worktree for those repos, without the operator having to select a worktree strategy per dispatch.
trigger: a repo has a treehouse.toml present at dispatch time
outcome: dispatch silently gets faster worktree acquisition once pooling has been set up once, with no per-dispatch flag needed
notes: Confirmed independently by sgt-dispatch's own worktree-strategy check (bin/sgt-dispatch L707-709): presence of treehouse.toml plus the treehouse binary selects the pool path.
rationale: A judgment/selection rule ('prefer treehouse when configured') that governs a step inside the dispatch procedure rather than being a bounded procedure of its own.

statement: Producing an agent's project-context orientation block resolves per-repo instructions by layering three sources in a fixed order — project-wide defaults, then the repo's group instructions, then the repo's own instructions — concatenating whichever of the three are actually present.
trigger: a repo is named or implied for an agent to work in
outcome: the agent receives one merged instruction block reflecting all three applicable layers, in a fixed precedence order
notes: Direct evidence for the ICM shared-context-map.md: this is the canonical instruction-layering resolution order the proposal's §9.4 example (AGENTS.md/agent-context BU) references.
rationale: A deterministic resolution algorithm reused wherever instructions must be merged (also echoed inside sgt-dispatch's own merged-instructions block); not itself a checkpoint.

statement: The generated context block reports each repo's clone status as one of exactly three states — cloned with its current branch, present but not a git repo, or not cloned at all — so a reading agent never has to infer clone state from absence.
trigger: a project context block is generated
outcome: the reported clone status is always one of three explicit, distinguishable states
rationale: A rule needed only while producing context; not independently invocable.

statement: If a project has a knowledge graph configured, the emitted context block tells the agent whether a built graph report already exists to read or names the exact command to build one, rather than silently omitting graph information.
trigger: a project has graphify.output configured
outcome: an agent orienting itself always knows whether an architecture graph is readable or must first be generated
rationale: A conditional detail surfaced while establishing scope, not a checkpoint of its own.

statement: A no-mistakes finding's severity and disposition together determine, deterministically, both its td priority and whether it is even allowed to be deferred: correctness/security/data-integrity/test findings must gate or ask the user and can never be routed to td or ignored, while cosmetic/evidence findings create no td card at all.
trigger: a no-mistakes review finding is classified with a kind and a requested disposition
outcome: a finding either blocks/escalates, is silently dropped as non-actionable, or is routed to td for later work — and which of those three happens is a deterministic function of kind, never left to caller discretion
notes: Named directly in the N1 contract's Method section as the no-mistakes stress case.
rationale: This is a meaningful durable checkpoint operators would care about (did this finding block, escalate, or become debt?) whose semantics (severity-kind → allowed dispositions) would survive reimplementation in any language — matches the §6.3 stage test verbatim.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected: the mapping is a fixed, reusable table, not a judgment call made anew per invocation)

statement: The disposition-to-severity table is a closed, deterministic mapping — gate or ask-user always becomes priority P1; td only accepts warning (P2) or informational (P3) severities; every other severity/disposition pairing is a hard error — so a caller cannot silently assign an unsupported combination.
trigger: a finding's disposition and severity are combined into a td priority
outcome: every accepted combination maps to exactly one priority, and every unaccepted combination is rejected rather than defaulted
rationale: A vocabulary/mapping table consumed by this router and echoed conceptually in sgt-review-findings' own severity/priority table; classify it as reusable shared vocabulary rather than a bounded procedure in its own right.

statement: Recording a no-mistakes finding as a td task is deduplicated by a stable marker embedded in the task description (no-mistakes-finding:<repo>:<finding-id>); if more than one existing td task carries the same marker the router refuses rather than picking one arbitrarily.
trigger: a finding is about to be recorded or updated in td
outcome: a finding maps to at most one td task, and an ambiguous match state is a hard failure rather than a silent pick
rationale: Deterministic deduplication machinery subordinate to the finding-disposition checkpoint.

statement: An existing td task matched by a finding's deduplication marker is reopened if closed and has its deferral cleared before being updated, so a finding that recurs after being closed or snoozed is never silently left in a stale closed/deferred state.
trigger: a finding matches an existing but closed or deferred td task
outcome: a recurring finding always surfaces as live tracked work again
rationale: A judgment rule attached to the finding-disposition checkpoint's td-routing sub-step, not a checkpoint by itself.

statement: A worker's free-text update message is classified into exactly one durable event kind — completion (done*/failed*), escalation (needs_input*/blocked*), or a generic update — purely by matching the message's leading token, and that classification, not the raw text, is what becomes the durable record.
trigger: a worker reports its status via sgt-notify
outcome: every notification is durably typed as completion, escalation, or update, independent of the message wording beyond its prefix
rationale: A meaningful durable checkpoint (what kind of event just happened) that operators and downstream automation both depend on; survives reimplementation regardless of transport (durable marker vs tmux injection).

statement: The durably recorded event (event=<kind>, updated=<timestamp> written under fleet state) is the source of truth for a worker update; any live delivery transport (e.g. injecting text into a tmux pane) is an optional compatibility layer on top, and its own failure to reach a coordinator must not be treated as failure to record the update.
trigger: a worker reports its status
outcome: the durable record of what happened exists and is correct regardless of whether any live notification transport succeeded
notes: Direct precursor to the proposal's invariant that work state is separate from execution/transport state (§4.2 analogue).
rationale: A broad rule about where truth lives (durable record over live transport) independent of any one procedure's stage — matches §6.1's own framing of invariants as stable and stage-independent.

statement: The compatibility tmux-injection transport for notifications is only attempted after confirming the recorded primary pane is a live tmux session; if the coordinator's session is gone but a durable callback origin was already registered, the transport degrades to 'queued for the durable callback' rather than failing the whole notification.
trigger: a live coordinator tmux session is required for the compatibility transport but is gone
outcome: a gone coordinator session degrades gracefully to durable-only delivery when a durable path exists, and only hard-fails when no durable path was ever registered
notes: Old mechanism (tmux send-keys into a specific pane) is superseded structurally by the daemon owning all client communication via the loopback API/SSE; the durable-fact-over-live-session precedence is the portable part.
rationale: The tmux-injection compatibility transport is exactly the class of mechanism the daemon's SSE/API surface replaces structurally (CLAUDE.md: clients reach state only through the API); nothing here needs to be reimplemented, though the graceful-degrade-to-durable-record principle it demonstrates is captured separately as an invariant.

statement: A worker completion or escalation notification is also written as a durable wiki activity entry distinguishing the completion/escalation heading and, when present, extracting and linking any GitHub PR URL mentioned in the message.
trigger: a worker update is being recorded
outcome: a durable, cross-referenced activity trail exists for every worker update independent of live delivery
notes: Overlaps skills/wiki/SKILL.md's captures convention (P5); this is the mechanism half that a wiki workflow's activity-capture stage would call.
rationale: A detail of what gets recorded at the classify-and-record checkpoint, not an independent checkpoint.

statement: Acknowledging a delivered response requires proof that the caller is the exact worker pane that owns this dispatch: the caller's own tmux pane, its recorded identity, and its exact fleet-recorded pane identity must all agree before any acknowledgement is accepted.
trigger: a worker attempts to acknowledge a delivered response
outcome: only the exact owning worker instance can ever acknowledge a response, never an impostor or a stale/relaunched pane
notes: Old mechanism (tmux pane identity matching) is superseded structurally by the daemon owning process identity exclusively (CLAUDE.md 'One owner'); the durable rule — a response transition may only be acknowledged by its verified owner — is the portable part.
rationale: Pane-identity comparison is tmux-specific mechanism the daemon's own process-handle ownership replaces structurally; the exactly-once-by-verified-owner property it enforces is durable and is captured in the response-publication behavior units instead.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected: too load-bearing/durable to be classified as merely a stage detail)

statement: A response can only be acknowledged when it is the exact pending response — matching response ID and a well-formed positive gate generation number — so an acknowledgement can never accidentally consume a different, superseding response.
trigger: a worker acknowledges a specific response by ID
outcome: an acknowledgement is bound to one exact response identity and generation, never a wildcard match
rationale: A durable checkpoint (a response is either the one being consumed or it is refused) whose exactly-once-by-identity semantics would survive reimplementation regardless of storage mechanism — matches §6.3.

statement: A response is archived as an evidence record only once the worker has produced explicit post-application proof matching the response's identity, gate generation, and current status, and the archived record's four fields (body, gate_generation, applied_status, proof) are published atomically via a staged temp directory renamed into place.
trigger: a response is being acknowledged for the first time
outcome: the archive can never claim a response was applied without the agent's own proof, and the archive entry is never observed half-written
notes: Direct precursor evidence for what a durable ExecutionRecord / delivered-response fact needs to contain (proposal §16.4-adjacent).
rationale: The four-field archive shape (body/gate_generation/applied_status/proof) is a durable record contract shared across sgt-ack-response (writer) and sgt-cleanup (validator/consumer), matching §6.6's shared-context test more than a single procedure's own checkpoint.

statement: An acknowledged response's terminal outcome must be internally consistent: a status of done requires a non-empty result already present, and a status of failed requires a non-blank reason string, or the acknowledgement is refused.
trigger: a response is being acknowledged against a terminal worker status
outcome: a terminal status is never accepted as evidence without the substance (result or reason) that makes it a real terminal outcome
rationale: A validation rule enforced at the acknowledge-response checkpoint, not a checkpoint of its own.

statement: Listing tracked work across a project defaults to showing only open tasks and can be narrowed by status, priority, or an explicit repo subset; every repo is queried independently and repos without an initialized task database are silently skipped rather than erroring the whole listing.
trigger: operator wants a unified view of tracked work across a project's repos
outcome: a filtered, unified view of open (or otherwise selected) tracked work across every configured repo
rationale: Bounded, independently invocable outcome; matches §6.2.

statement: Creating tracked-work items across several repos for one cross-repo brief is all-or-nothing: every target repo is validated up front (cloned, task tracker initialized) before any task is created, and if creating a task in any repo fails after some were already created, every already-created task is deleted to roll back.
trigger: a cross-repo brief needs one tracked-work item per target repo
outcome: either every target repo ends with exactly one new task, or none of them do — never a partial set left behind
notes: Adjacent-append-crash-window-style hazard, applied to cross-process task creation rather than the journal.
rationale: A durable checkpoint (all-or-nothing multi-repo task creation) operators would care about regardless of mechanism — matches §6.3.

statement: Recording a worker's handoff or response-provenance evidence in the task tracker refuses to run unless the calling process's argument path is verified to be the exact worktree root the fleet state already recorded as owned, rather than trusting the caller's current working directory.
trigger: a worker exit or response event needs its git identity recorded in the task tracker
outcome: tracked-work evidence never gets attached to the wrong repository's git identity, even though the recording tool itself binds identity to process cwd
notes: Documents a measured defect in the underlying tool (td binds git metadata to process cwd, not --work-dir) and the compensating verify-then-cd-in workaround; explicitly says the comment 'cannot outlive its evidence' (tests/sgt-td-memory-worktree-test.sh, P7).
rationale: Deterministic verify-then-invoke machinery reused by both sgt-watch and sgt-respond, subordinate to whichever checkpoint calls it (worker exit, response acknowledgement); not itself a checkpoint.

statement: Recording that a human response was delivered to a worker never writes the actual response text into the task tracker; only the response's opaque identifier and a note that the exact text was delivered through a separate atomic transport are logged, keeping response content out of the tracked-work history.
trigger: a human response has been delivered to a worker
outcome: the task tracker gets an auditable pointer to the fact a response happened, never the response content itself
notes: Direct precedent for keeping potentially sensitive response content out of a durable, more widely-read log while still recording that a decision occurred.
rationale: A broad, stage-independent content-handling rule (don't put response text in the shared tracker) rather than a checkpoint or helper — matches §6.1's framing of standing rules about authority/evidence boundaries.

statement: Force-stopping workers is refused unless a cooperative drain is already active for the targeted scope, and it always requires explicit confirmation (--yes) or is limited to a --dry-run preview; it never runs automatically as a side effect of anything else.
trigger: cooperative drain has failed to stop some workers within a bounded wait
outcome: a destructive force-stop only ever happens as an explicit, confirmed, drain-scoped operator action with full identity disclosed first
rationale: A destructive, human-authorized checkpoint operators would explicitly want to observe/gate — matches §6.3/§6.4 (requires judgment: an operator decision to force).

statement: Before signalling a recorded worker PID, force-stop verifies the process's recorded start time still matches its actual start time, so a PID that has since been reused by an unrelated process is recognized and treated as already-gone rather than being killed.
trigger: force-stop is about to signal a recorded worker PID
outcome: force-stop never kills an unrelated process that happens to have inherited a recycled PID
notes: Same PID-reuse-detection pattern recurs across sgt-drain, sgt-recover, sgt-cleanup — a shared safety property of every process-identity check in this codebase.
rationale: A verification technique reused across every process-termination path in this partition; deterministic machinery, not itself a checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (rejected: too mechanism-specific — PID/start-time comparison — to state as a stage-independent rule)

statement: Force-stopping a worker also stops any live Claude background session recorded for it before signalling the worker's own process, because a background Claude session is not a child of the worker's process group and is invisible to process-group signals.
trigger: a worker being force-stopped may have a live Claude background session
outcome: no Claude background session is left running after a worker it belonged to is force-stopped
notes: D2 confirms sergeant-rs's headless print-mode Claude turns have no equivalent detached background-session concept; this whole backstop class is obsolete-mechanism for the D2-superseded `claude --bg` model.
rationale: Ties directly to the already-superseded Claude Background Harness mechanism (D2); the durable underlying rule — every termination path must account for out-of-process-group resources it created — is worth noting in obsolete-mechanisms.md but the mechanism itself does not need to be reimplemented.

statement: Before invoking the shipping-gate tool, the validation worker re-reads and re-hashes the canonical intent file and refuses to proceed if its content changed since the coordinator's own initial verification, so a content edit made in the gap between launch and run is caught rather than silently validated.
trigger: the validation worker is about to invoke no-mistakes
outcome: the intent that gates a validation run is guaranteed byte-identical to the intent verified at launch, with no window for a late substitution
notes: Same content-hash-revisioning technique as _sgt-intent.sh's _sgt_intent_revision, applied at the last possible moment before use.
rationale: A judgment/verification rule attached to the launch-and-run checkpoint, not a checkpoint of its own.

statement: The validation worker only proceeds while its recorded coordinator is provably still alive (matching PID and process-start time), polling that liveness before every synchronization handshake step, so an orphaned validation run never blocks forever waiting on a coordinator that already died.
trigger: the validation worker is waiting on a coordinator handshake step
outcome: a dead coordinator is detected promptly instead of the worker waiting indefinitely
rationale: PID/process-start liveness polling of a coordinator is exactly the class of mechanism the daemon's single-owner process model (CLAUDE.md 'One owner') removes the need for — there is no separate long-lived coordinator process to go stale in the daemon's actor-stage execution model.

statement: The isolated validation code snapshot's identity is re-verified against the reviewed commit immediately before invoking the shipping-gate tool — the snapshot must still be at the exact reviewed HEAD and have a clean tree — so validation can never silently run against code that changed after review.
trigger: the validation worker is about to invoke no-mistakes against the isolated snapshot
outcome: the exact code that was reviewed is the exact code that gets validated — no substitution window
notes: Directly analogous to CLAUDE.md's own gate discipline: a shipping decision must be about the code actually reviewed, never a moving target.
rationale: A verification rule attached to the launch checkpoint, not an independent checkpoint.

statement: Which intent-transport mechanism (a private file path vs. exposing content in argv) is used for a validation run is decided once by the coordinator and then honored exactly by the worker, never re-optimized at run time even if a different transport would now also work.
trigger: the validation worker is about to build its invocation of no-mistakes
outcome: an operator's earlier consent (or non-consent) to exposing intent content via argv can never be silently upgraded or downgraded between launch and run
rationale: A stage-independent authority/consent rule (a recorded operator decision is honored exactly, never re-decided by machinery) — matches §6.1's framing of preserving authority boundaries.

statement: Because no-mistakes exposes its accepted flags only through its own --help output, whether a given no-mistakes build supports a capability is determined by parsing that help text, never by inferring support from a version number.
trigger: Sergeant needs to know whether the installed no-mistakes build supports a given flag
outcome: capability decisions are grounded in the actual installed binary's declared surface, not an assumption tied to a version string
notes: Directly relevant to the proposal's §17 Harness Registry/doctor design: 'measure the CLI' rather than assume from docs/version (L1-adjacent).
rationale: A broad, stage-independent rule about how capability must be established (measured from the real binary, never assumed) — directly parallels §6.1's 'every advertised capability is measured' framing that also appears as CLAUDE.md invariant 4.8.

statement: There are exactly two intent-content transports to a validation run — a private file path, whose content never appears in process argv or /proc, versus argv, which exposes content through ps and /proc — and the argv transport is only ever selected when the operator has explicitly consented.
trigger: a validation run needs to pass its canonical intent to no-mistakes
outcome: intent content is never exposed through argv/proc unless the operator explicitly opted in
rationale: A stage-independent privacy/consent rule governing every place intent reaches an external process, not one checkpoint's detail.

statement: An objective whose text matches a fixed set of safety-sensitive or stateful keywords (auth, security, secrets, payments, databases, migrations, production, destructive, persistent state, state transitions) cannot proceed on the standard-isolated intent path and must instead be given an explicit --intent-file.
trigger: a work objective is being auto-converted into a minimal standard-isolated intent
outcome: risky-sounding work can never proceed on the lightweight auto-generated intent path; it must be given an explicit, fuller intent document
rationale: A durable checkpoint (does this work require the full intent-authoring path or the minimal one?) that operators would want measured/gated regardless of implementation — matches §6.3.

statement: A canonical intent document is only ever valid if it contains exactly eight required sections, in a fixed order, each with non-empty content — Objective, Required Invariants, Approved Tradeoffs, Out Of Scope, State Transitions, Failure Windows, Negative Test Matrix, Validation Evidence.
trigger: an intent document is prepared or supplied
outcome: every intent document Sergeant will act on has the same fixed, complete shape, or it is rejected before being used
notes: Direct precursor to proposal §9.4-9.5's own record-shape discipline (fixed required fields, machine-checkable).
rationale: A canonical document schema consumed by multiple procedures (dispatch's intent preparation, sgt-respond's revision matching, sgt-validate's launch) with the same contract everywhere — matches §6.6.

statement: An intent file path is refused if it contains newline/carriage-return characters, attempts path traversal, traverses any symlink component, exceeds 65536 bytes, or contains control characters other than tab and newline — before its content is even read for the schema check.
trigger: an operator supplies an intent file via --intent-file
outcome: a malicious or malformed intent path can never smuggle content or escape the expected file location
rationale: Deterministic, reusable input-hardening machinery consumed anywhere an intent path is accepted from an operator; not itself a checkpoint.

statement: A consumed response is durably archived as exactly four fields in one directory — body (the exact response transport), gate_generation, applied_status, and proof (the worker's own post-application record) — and every reader of that archive is required to go through the same shared parsing helpers so the format has exactly one definition.
trigger: a response has been consumed by a worker
outcome: what counts as proof that a response was delivered and applied is defined exactly once and shared by every producer/consumer
notes: This is the exact four-field shape a §9.4-style behavior-unit record for 'delivered response' evidence would need to preserve.
rationale: Canonical shared record shape consumed by three independent scripts (sgt-ack-response, sgt-cleanup, this file itself); matches §6.6 exactly.

statement: Mutual-exclusion locking uses a hard link, not flock(1) or mkdir, specifically because flock is unavailable on macOS system installs and limited on BusyBox, and because a hard link publishes the lock together with its owner record in one atomic step so it can never exist unattributably.

source.locator: L126-132 (this rationale governs the identical hard-link lock design in bin/_sgt-response-lock.sh)

trigger: two processes may contend for the same response lock
outcome: mutual exclusion holds correctly across every platform Sergeant supports, with a lock that is always attributable to a specific owner
notes: Same rationale is stated at bin/_sgt-drain.sh's admission lock (identical hard-link-not-flock design, shared verbatim across the two lock implementations in this partition) — the locator cites the canonical statement of the rationale.
rationale: Deterministic, cross-platform-portable locking machinery reused by every response-touching script (sgt-respond, sgt-recover, sgt-ack-response, sgt-review-findings, sgt-watch) — matches §6.6's shared-helper test precisely.

statement: A lock whose recorded owner PID is no longer alive is reclaimed automatically by the next contender, rather than requiring manual intervention, because release is a caller-side write rather than a kernel-held handle and a killed holder would otherwise leave the lock stuck forever.

source.locator: L148-152 (this released-vs-kernel-held rationale governs the identical lock design in bin/_sgt-response-lock.sh)

trigger: a lock holder is killed while holding the lock
outcome: a crashed holder never leaves the lock permanently stuck; the next contender can always recover it once liveness is disproven
rationale: A stage-independent durability property (a lock is recoverable from any crash) that must hold across every use of this locking primitive; matches §6.1's framing of broad, rarely-changing rules.

statement: An action-lease outcome for a delivered notification is recorded exactly once and never overwritten by a later finalization attempt, so the first, most-proximate reason a lease was settled or left pending survives every later retry.
trigger: a notification's action lease is being finalized or reported as still pending
outcome: the audit trail for why a lease is settled or outstanding is stable and never gets silently rewritten by a subsequent attempt
rationale: Deterministic write-once evidence machinery reused wherever a lease outcome is recorded (worker exit, drain handoff, recovery convergence); subordinate to whichever checkpoint calls it.

statement: An action lease is only ever settled as completed from the agent's own durable proof, written as exactly '<notification_id>|<lease>' at a fixed location; nothing may fabricate completion from an inference (e.g. 'the pane looks idle') — a mismatched identity, nonce, missing target, or absent proof always fails closed and is recorded as pending with its reason.
trigger: a notification's action lease is being finalized
outcome: no notification is ever recorded as delivered-and-acted-on without the acting agent's own exact proof for that turn
notes: Direct precursor for what an ExecutionRecord's completion evidence must require: the actor's own proof, never an inference from process state.
rationale: A stage-independent evidence-integrity rule (never fabricate completion) that governs every place delivery/completion is claimed — matches §6.1's 'preserve source history and authority boundaries' framing and CLAUDE.md's 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant applied to notification evidence specifically.

statement: Settling a delivered notification's completion is safely reentrant: if the calling context already holds the response lock it keeps ownership and is responsible for releasing it, and if another context in the same process holds it, waiting is recognized as futile (the liveness check would see this process's own live PID forever) and the attempt is deferred to the exit boundary instead of spinning.
trigger: one process has multiple concurrent contexts (background loops) that might all try to finalize the same lease
outcome: a self-deadlock (waiting on your own process's live PID) can never happen; the finalization is always eventually attempted at a point where it can succeed
rationale: A deterministic reentrancy rule inside the shared lease-finalization helper, subordinate to whatever checkpoint calls it.

statement: Whether admission (new dispatch or relaunch) is currently allowed is decided purely by the presence of a drain file — global or project-scoped — and an empty or unparseable project name is treated as absent, checking only the global drain rather than erroring.
trigger: a new dispatch or relaunch is about to happen
outcome: admission is blocked exactly when a global or a matching project drain exists, and never ambiguously blocked or admitted by a malformed project name
rationale: A meaningful, durable checkpoint (is new work admitted right now?) whose file-existence-based semantics would survive reimplementation — matches §6.3.

statement: A concurrent 'read drain state, then start a new pane' race is closed by an explicit admission lock that every dispatch/relaunch path (sgt-dispatch, sgt-respond) and every drain-set/undrain path (sgt-drain) must acquire before reading or writing drain state, so a drain set mid-dispatch is never silently missed.
trigger: a dispatch/relaunch and a drain-set could happen concurrently
outcome: admission decisions are always made against a consistent, lock-serialized view of drain state — never a stale read that lets new work slip through a just-activated drain
rationale: A concurrency-correctness rule attached to the check-admission checkpoint, not a checkpoint of its own; the lock mechanism itself is a shared-helper (captured separately).

statement: A lock's recorded owner is only ever declared 'provably gone' — and therefore reclaimable — when the record names this exact host and a PID that is either confirmed not running or confirmed to have been reused by a different process; an unidentified host, a foreign host, a missing/malformed record, or undeterminable liveness always keeps the lock intact.
trigger: a contender wants to determine whether a held lock can be reclaimed
outcome: a live lock can never be stolen out from under its true owner; only a positively-proven-dead owner's lock is ever reclaimed
rationale: Deterministic, cross-platform liveness-proof machinery reused by every lock in this partition (response lock, drain admission lock, validation launch lock all restate this same fail-closed reclamation rule); matches §6.6.

statement: A lock reclamation binds itself to the exact stale instance it proved dead via a unique nonce, and re-checks that nonce after atomically renaming the record aside, so a lock that was legitimately reacquired by its true owner between the staleness decision and the rename is restored rather than destroyed.
trigger: a contender is reclaiming a lock it proved is stale
outcome: a reclamation can never destroy a lock instance that is not the exact one it proved stale, even under a race
rationale: Deterministic race-safe reclamation machinery, part of the same shared locking primitive as the owner-is-gone check.

statement: Every lock acquisition timeout report names the specific owner (PID, user, host, purpose, age) and the exact recovery action, because an undiagnosable 'could not acquire lock' failure is not actionable for an operator.
trigger: a lock could not be acquired within its bound
outcome: an operator facing a contended lock always sees who holds it and how to proceed, never a bare failure
rationale: A stage-independent diagnosability standard (failures must name the cause and the remedy) applicable to every timeout/failure path in this partition, not one checkpoint's detail.

statement: A drain-lock acquisition failure that stems from the filesystem itself being unable to create hard links (e.g. FAT/exFAT, some CIFS/FUSE mounts) is distinguished from ordinary contention, because spinning to the deadline and reporting 'contended' would send an operator chasing a holder that does not exist.
trigger: the lock filesystem does not support hard links
outcome: an environment-incompatibility failure is reported immediately and correctly, never masquerading as ordinary lock contention
rationale: A specific fail-fast rule attached to the locking machinery used at the check-admission checkpoint; too narrow to be its own stage.

statement: A cooperative drain of a scope is a bounded wait, not an instantaneous switch: workers already running are asked to finish their current turn and exit, new admission is refused immediately, and the wait bound reports every unresolved worker by exact identity on timeout while leaving them running rather than terminating anything.
trigger: an operator drains a project or the whole fleet, optionally waiting for convergence
outcome: either the scope reaches a fully-drained state within the bound, or the operator gets a precise, actionable report of exactly what is still outstanding — with nothing ever force-terminated by this path
notes: This is a distinct, engine-relevant capability from sgt-drain-force: the current sergeant-rs daemon has no documented 'block new stage admission, bounded-wait for in-flight turns to finish naturally, report unresolved by name, never terminate' operator-declared maintenance mode.
rationale: Old Sergeant's mechanism (tmux pane liveness polling) is obsolete, but the underlying capability — an operator-declared, durable, queryable admission-block that coexists with in-flight work finishing naturally and reports unresolved work by name — is not obviously represented anywhere in the proposal's Phase-B execute-stage semantics (§15, which covers per-execution cancellation/timeout, not fleet-wide graceful admission control).
alternatives_considered: Represent drain as ordinary stage-context inside every dispatch/execute path (rejected: admission-blocking must be observable and durable independent of any single Work, and must persist across daemon restarts)

Implement drain purely client-side by having the CLI simply stop issuing new work (rejected: does not block a second operator/client from admitting new work, and provides no durable, queryable 'drained' state)

engine_gap.behavior: An operator-declared, durable, scope-qualified (global or per-project) admission block that (a) refuses new stage/turn admission the instant it is set, (b) never terminates in-flight work, (c) supports a bounded wait that converges when every in-flight turn in scope finishes naturally, and (d) on timeout reports precisely which turns are still unresolved by identity.
engine_gap.evidence: bin/sgt-drain, bin/_sgt-drain.sh (admission lock + drain files), and bin/sgt-drain-force (the confirmed, drain-scoped escape hatch) together implement roughly 1,100 lines of file-based admission-control and liveness-verification state with no equivalent concept described in the read sections of the proposal's runtime/execution model.
lower_rungs_attempted: A helper an actor stage calls to check 'should I start' (§6.5)
A per-Work cancellation/timeout mechanism (§15.5/§15.6 of the proposal)
why_each_fails: A per-stage helper check cannot durably and atomically block admission fleet-wide against a concurrent dispatch racing to start — that is exactly the admission-lock race the old mechanism exists to close, and a stage-local helper has no cross-Work visibility to close it.

Cancellation/timeout (§15.5/§15.6) governs one execution's own lifecycle; it has no concept of 'block starting NEW executions across the whole daemon or one project, while leaving already-running ones alone', which is the entire point of a drain.
engine_gap.minimum_capability_required: The runtime itself must own a durable, queryable admission-block fact (global or project-scoped) that every stage-launch path consults atomically before starting a new execution, plus a way to enumerate in-flight executions in scope so a bounded wait can report exactly what remains.
engine_gap.acceptance_test: Setting a project-scoped drain immediately causes any subsequent stage-launch attempt for that project to be refused (observable via the API) while a currently-running stage for that project is left running to completion; querying drain status during the wait lists the still-running stage by Work/stage identity, and clearing the drain restores admission without needing to touch any in-flight execution.

statement: A worker is only ever counted as having genuinely finished draining when its recorded process is provably gone; absence of recorded identity is explicitly not treated as proof of exit, so an unverifiable worker blocks a drain wait rather than being silently counted as resolved.
trigger: a bounded drain wait is evaluating whether the scope is fully drained
outcome: a drain wait can never falsely report success because a worker's identity happened to be unrecordable
rationale: Fail-closed judgment rule attached to the await-drained checkpoint's liveness evidence, not a checkpoint of its own (the checkpoint itself is the engine-gap unit above).

statement: Every accepted interactive harness's capability gate, readiness probe, and launch arguments are driven from one single registry, replacing three previously separately-maintained definitions that had drifted apart until one harness was accepted and launchable while permanently unable to satisfy readiness.
trigger: an interactive harness must be gated, probed for readiness, and launched consistently
outcome: a harness cannot ship accepted without a readiness probe, and the three decisions can never drift apart again because they share one data source
notes: Explicitly flagged in source-inventory as engine-pressure evidence for proposal §17 (Harness Registry/doctor): 'one registry, not three drifting definitions' is a portable design principle even though the tmux-pane mechanism itself is obsolete.
rationale: A single canonical registry consumed by the capability gate, the readiness check, and the launch-argv assembly — the textbook §6.6 shared-helper pattern (one source of truth for several consumers).
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (the underlying 'one registry, not three drifting definitions' principle is closer to an invariant, captured as a separate unit)

statement: One registry not three drifting definitions is itself the durable design principle worth preserving independent of the specific harness/tmux mechanism: any capability that gates admission, is probed for readiness, and is then invoked must derive all three decisions from the same single declaration, never three independently maintained ones.
trigger: any future capability class (harness, backend, execution adapter) needs a gate + probe + invocation
outcome: drift between what is accepted, what is checked as ready, and what is actually invoked becomes structurally impossible
notes: This is the portable design lesson the source-inventory row for this file explicitly calls out as engine-pressure evidence for §17.
rationale: Broad, stage-independent design rule extractable from the mechanism, matching §6.1's own framing — 'do not silently substitute a harness' generalizes to 'do not let gate/probe/invoke definitions drift apart'.
alternatives_considered: shared-helper (the concrete registry implementation, captured separately)

statement: Readiness for an interactive harness answers exactly one question — will a keystroke sent now reach a running harness rather than being swallowed during startup — and is deliberately defined without any UI presentation-string match or harness-name comparison, because both have already been measured to break across harness UI revisions and across interpreted-language harnesses.
trigger: a supervisor needs to know whether it is safe to deliver a notification to an interactive harness pane
outcome: readiness detection is robust to UI text changes and to harnesses whose process name is an interpreter, not the harness itself
notes: Old mechanism (tmux pane rendering inspection) is obsolete under D2's headless-turn model, where there is no interactive pane to probe at all — a `claude -p` turn either produces output or it doesn't, with no 'is it ready to receive a keystroke' question.
rationale: Readiness-via-pane-inspection is structurally replaced by the headless print-mode turn model (D2): there is no long-lived interactive pane in the daemon's execution model for a keystroke to reach. The measured failure modes (presentation-string fragility, interpreter-name mismatch) are recorded so a future TUI/attach-style feature does not repeat them.

statement: Readiness requires the harness to be observed rendering on two consecutive probes, not merely once, because a TUI that has just painted its first frame may still be installing its input handlers; requiring two observations rather than a fixed wall-clock delay scales naturally with whatever polling interval the caller already uses.
trigger: a harness pane has just rendered its first visible frame
outcome: a nudge is never delivered to a harness that only just started rendering and may still be initializing input handling
rationale: Same D2-superseded interactive-pane mechanism; noted so the two-observations-over-fixed-delay technique is not lost if a future interactive/TUI feature reintroduces a similar readiness question.

statement: Every row in the harness registry must be validated — well-formed shape, a declared probe that is actually implemented, and no harness declared twice — before the capability gate is trusted, so a newly accepted harness can never ship without a working readiness probe.
trigger: the capability gate is about to decide whether a harness is accepted
outcome: an inconsistent registry is caught immediately, by name, rather than silently accepting an unusable harness
rationale: Deterministic self-validation machinery for the shared registry; subordinate to whichever checkpoint (harness launch) consults the registry.

statement: The opencode/oc harnesses are launched with a permission-bypass flag as a deliberate security posture: Sergeant workers execute in an automated dispatch context with no human at the keyboard to answer interactive permission prompts, so operator trust is scoped instead to the intent file and worker brief reviewed and approved at dispatch time.
trigger: an autonomous interactive worker is launched via opencode/oc
outcome: autonomous execution is authorized once, in advance, via the reviewed intent/brief, rather than requiring per-action human confirmation that cannot happen in an unattended dispatch
notes: Directly relevant to how sergeant-rs's own headless `claude -p` turns are authorized: the underlying principle (authorization is scoped to the reviewed intent, not per-action prompts) is portable even though the specific flag/harness is not.
rationale: A stage-independent authorization-model rule (where does the operator's consent for autonomous action actually live) — matches §6.1's authority-boundary framing, not a single checkpoint's detail.

statement: A stall recovery attempt is gated on concrete stall proof — status must be in_progress and the fleet diagnostic must begin with a stall-classification marker written by the watcher — and every invocation is stamped so a second attempt always escalates to needs_input instead of retrying, guaranteeing exactly one bounded relaunch.
trigger: a worker's status is in_progress with a recorded stall diagnostic
outcome: a stalled worker gets exactly one automatic relaunch attempt, ever, before requiring human input
rationale: A meaningful, bounded, exactly-once durable checkpoint operators would want measured (was recovery attempted? did it succeed or escalate?) — matches §6.3.

statement: During recovery, the replacement worker is only launched, and its identity validated, before the original stalled pane is ever killed, so that any failure in the relaunch sequence leaves the original stalled process intact for investigation rather than losing the supervisor entirely.
trigger: a stall recovery attempt is relaunching a worker
outcome: a failed recovery attempt never leaves a Work with no supervisor at all
rationale: An ordering rule that governs the recovery checkpoint's safe execution, not an independent checkpoint.

statement: A recovery attempt refuses to proceed while an unfinished notification action-lease exists, unless the lease's owner is provably dead (its pane no longer resolves at all and its recorded process is not running) — anything else, including a pane that merely looks idle, must fail closed to preserve exact-once delivery evidence.
trigger: a stall-recovery attempt finds an outstanding action lease from the stalled worker
outcome: recovery either converges the lease from the agent's own proof, proceeds only after proving the owner is truly dead, or refuses and escalates — never silently discards pending delivery evidence
notes: A prior version of this rule refused unconditionally, which made a worker holding a dead supervisor's lease permanently unrecoverable — the convergence-then-provably-dead-adjudication design is the fix.
rationale: A fail-closed judgment rule attached to the recovery checkpoint's pre-flight evidence-preservation step.

statement: Before relaunching a stalled worker's Claude session, recovery first checks whether the stalled worker left a live background session and stops it, guaranteed to happen before the replacement is dispatched, so two Claude processes are never concurrently running against the same worktree.
trigger: a stalled Claude worker is about to be relaunched
outcome: exactly one process is ever active against a given worktree, even across a relaunch
notes: D2-superseded mechanism (claude --bg background sessions do not exist under headless print-mode turns), but the underlying invariant — never run two concurrent processes against the same worktree across a relaunch — is durable and portable.
rationale: The specific stop-then-dispatch ordering exists only because of the D2-superseded background-session mechanism; a headless `-p`/`--resume` model has no equivalent detached process to stop, since a turn's process exits when the turn ends. The 'never two concurrent processes on one worktree across a relaunch' rule it enforces is worth preserving conceptually.

statement: A recovery attempt runs every pre-flight validation — stall proof, lease convergence, drain check, relaunch-metadata completeness, old-pane identity — to completion before stamping the attempt as made, so that any pre-flight failure leaves the stalled worker untouched and eligible for a real recovery attempt later.
trigger: a stall recovery is being attempted
outcome: a recovery attempt is 'used up' (the one-shot budget consumed) only once the coordinator has actually committed to relaunching, never by a pre-flight check that merely failed to validate
rationale: An ordering discipline governing the recovery checkpoint, not a checkpoint of its own.

statement: Delivering a response to a live, identity-verified worker pane is bounded by a fixed acknowledgement timeout; when that bound elapses the response remains durably stored but unconsumed, and a documented recovery path — rerunning the exact same command — performs exactly one bounded worker relaunch rather than leaving the operator with no supported next action.
trigger: a delivered response is not acknowledged within the bound
outcome: an unresponsive worker never permanently strands a pending response; the operator always has one supported, bounded next action
notes: Records a measured defect (a documented dead-end) and its fix; this exact bounded-timeout-then-relaunch pattern is what a headless print-mode turn model makes unnecessary, since a turn either completes or the process exits — there is no separate 'acknowledge the notification' step for a `-p` invocation.
rationale: The delivery/acknowledgement split this rule exists to bound is a structural artifact of the persistent-pane worker model; a headless turn model (D2) collapses delivery and consumption into one process invocation, removing the class of failure this rule compensates for. The 'never leave the operator with no supported next action' principle is worth preserving as a general design lesson.

statement: Responding to a worker whose recorded worktree ownership marker no longer matches attempts a one-time, tightly-scoped legacy-state migration — re-deriving and cross-checking git pointer, branch, brief content, and project configuration identity — before failing; the migration only ever writes fields that were previously absent, never overwriting anything already recorded.
trigger: fleet state predates the worktree-ownership-marker fields this script now expects
outcome: pre-existing fleet state can be brought forward to the current ownership contract without an operator having to manually patch files, but only when every cross-check independently agrees
notes: A schema-migration technique for durable state; the specific field set (worktree_git_pointer, worktree_git_dir, .sergeant-intent.md placement) is tmux/worktree-file-specific and obsolete under the daemon's own journal-backed WorkRun state.
rationale: The migrated fields are all file-based worktree/fleet-state artifacts specific to the old implementation; the daemon's journal-as-only-truth model has no equivalent 'legacy on-disk marker' concept to migrate. The write-only-if-absent, verify-every-cross-check-independently caution is the durable lesson worth preserving in obsolete-mechanisms.md.

statement: A response can only ever be published against a worker whose current status is needs_input, blocked, waiting, or orphaned — any other status refuses the response outright, so a response is never silently applied to a worker that was not actually asking for one.
trigger: an operator supplies a response for a specific task/repo
outcome: responses are only ever delivered to workers in one of exactly four states that legitimately mean 'this worker is waiting for input'
rationale: A durable checkpoint (is this worker even eligible for a response right now?) whose semantics would survive reimplementation — matches §6.3.

statement: An outstanding notification action-lease from the worker being responded to is first attempted to converge through the one shared finalizer, using only the agent's own exact completion proof; only if that convergence fails does responding refuse with a specific remediation pointing at the exact evidence path.
trigger: a response relaunch would otherwise clear an outstanding action lease
outcome: a legitimate but unrecorded completion is never discarded by a relaunch, and a genuinely unfinished lease is refused with a concrete remediation, never silently overwritten
rationale: Fail-closed evidence-preservation rule attached to the relaunch checkpoint.

statement: A response relaunch never allows a second, superseding tmux pane to displace the first without preserving the first pane's superseded notification-target identity as evidence — and if that evidence would conflict with already-recorded evidence, the relaunch refuses outright rather than losing the older evidence.
trigger: a relaunch is superseding an existing notification target
outcome: the evidence trail for who was ever asked to act, and when they were superseded, is never lost or silently overwritten
rationale: Fail-closed evidence-preservation rule attached to the relaunch checkpoint; the same class of rule as the action-lease convergence unit above.

statement: Before dispatching a replacement worker during a response-driven relaunch, the superseded worker's live Claude background session is stopped first, guaranteed by ordering (the liveness check runs before the new pane is created) so two processes never run concurrently against the same worktree.
trigger: a response relaunch is about to dispatch a replacement worker
outcome: exactly one process is ever active against a worktree, even across a response-driven relaunch
notes: Same D2-superseded pattern as sgt-recover's prior-session check.
rationale: D2-superseded background-session mechanism; headless single-turn-per-process execution makes concurrent-session collision structurally impossible without needing a stop-then-dispatch check.

statement: Independent review findings are routed to tracked work as a bounded, evidence-preserving procedure: parse and sanitize the reviewer's structured output, retain a sanitized copy before any external side effect, route each actionable finding to exactly one deduplicated task, and — only once every finding has reached tracked work — publish a blocking gate if any finding is severe enough to block, or clear it otherwise.
trigger: a review pass (standards, spec, readiness, etc.) produces structured findings
outcome: every actionable finding either reaches exactly one tracked-work item or is explicitly refused with a stated reason; a severe-enough finding blocks the worker until it is addressed
rationale: Recognizable trigger (a review completes) and bounded, independently invocable outcome (findings are either routed or explicitly refused, and the worker's blocked state reflects the routing outcome) — matches §6.2.

statement: Only the error-family severities publish a blocking gate; warning and info severities always route as reviewable debt (a tracked task) without ever blocking the worker.
trigger: a finding's severity determines whether it blocks
outcome: the worker is only ever blocked by findings severe enough to matter, and non-blocking findings are never dropped, only deferred as tracked debt
rationale: A severity-to-consequence vocabulary sourced from bin/_sgt-review-axes.sh and consumed by this router, the brief template, and the worker-brief contract alike — matches §6.6.

statement: A retained, sanitized artifact of parsed findings is written to durable storage before any external side effect (td calls), so a routing failure that happens after parsing never destroys the only copy of a review's findings; the artifact's location is included in the failure diagnostic as an explicit, retryable next action.
trigger: findings have been parsed and validated, before they are routed to td
outcome: a review's evidence is never lost to a downstream infrastructural failure; it is always retryable from a durable, redacted copy
rationale: A durable checkpoint (findings are retained before any external write) operators would care about independent of mechanism, matching §6.3.

statement: A finding is deduplicated against an existing tracked-work item using a marker scoped to the exact review axis, source, finding ID, parent mission, and branch — never axis/source/id alone — because reviewers emit generic finding IDs (e.g. 'spec-1') that would otherwise collide across unrelated review sessions and let one session's update silently overwrite another's evidence.
trigger: a finding is being matched against previously routed findings
outcome: findings from genuinely different review sessions are never conflated into one tracked-work item just because they share a generic id
rationale: A specific deduplication-scope rule attached to the routing checkpoint, not an independent checkpoint.

statement: A matched existing tracked-work item is only ever updated (priority, labels reopened-if-closed) when its stored content digest still matches the incoming finding's digest; a divergent stored body is refused and left completely untouched — no description, title, or status change — so nothing stored can ever be silently lost by a write that never happens.
trigger: a deduplication match's stored content digest disagrees with the incoming finding
outcome: a mismatched match is refused explicitly rather than silently overwriting potentially human-edited or differently-sourced evidence
rationale: A fail-closed write-integrity rule attached to the routing checkpoint's per-finding update step.

statement: Sensitive-looking content is redacted from every review finding field before it is ever written anywhere — secret-shaped key=value pairs, bearer/basic auth headers, known token formats (GitHub, AWS), credentialed URLs, PEM private-key markers, and generic high-entropy strings all get replaced with a redaction marker.
trigger: a review finding's text fields are being parsed
outcome: a review that accidentally surfaces credential-shaped material never propagates it into a tracked-work item
rationale: Deterministic sanitization machinery applied uniformly to every finding field; a reusable safety technique, not a checkpoint by itself.

statement: Publishing a freshly built project knowledge graph is atomic: concurrent readers see either the complete old graph or the complete new graph throughout the whole run, never a partial or missing state, regardless of whether the configured output is a plain directory or a symlink pointing inside or outside a source repo.
trigger: a project's knowledge graph is rebuilt
outcome: the published graph is always internally consistent and complete at every point in time, never observed half-written
rationale: A durable checkpoint (graph publication either fully succeeded or the old graph is still intact) whose atomicity would matter under any implementation — matches §6.3.

statement: Extracting a repo's graph data stages the repo into a filtered, non-source-repo scratch location before scanning whenever any output-exclusion pattern applies, so the extraction tool can never re-ingest an already-published graph nested inside the source repo it is scanning.
trigger: a repo's graph output lives nested inside the repo itself
outcome: a graph build never accidentally indexes its own previous output as source material
rationale: A filtering rule needed only while extracting one repo, not a checkpoint of its own.

statement: When no supported LLM API key is configured, graph extraction is run in code-only mode rather than being allowed to abort the entire multi-repo run on encountering a non-code file it cannot semantically process without a key.
trigger: no supported LLM API key is available in the environment
outcome: graph extraction degrades gracefully to code-only indexing rather than aborting the whole project graph build
rationale: An environment-sensing degrade rule attached to the extraction checkpoint.

statement: Building a project graph across many repos is all-or-nothing at the merge step: if extraction fails for any included repo, the whole run fails before attempting to merge or publish anything, rather than publishing a graph silently missing some repos.
trigger: one or more repos fail extraction during a multi-repo graph build
outcome: a published project graph is always complete over every repo it claims to cover, never silently partial
rationale: A durable checkpoint (was the graph build complete before anything was published?) that matters regardless of implementation — matches §6.3.

statement: Synthesizing a daily activity digest is a bounded procedure that collects session content from every configured AI-agent history source for one day (silently skipping any source that is unavailable), enriches it with merged pull requests and completed tracked-work items for that day, and produces one synthesized markdown page per day rather than a raw log dump.
trigger: operator or a scheduled job wants a synthesized record of a day's work
outcome: one durable, synthesized (not raw) markdown page per day, cross-linked into the wiki index
notes: Overlaps skills/wiki/SKILL.md (P5), which owns the wiki convention this script implements the mechanism for.
rationale: Bounded, independently invocable outcome (one digest page per day) with its own completion condition (skip if already written) — matches §6.2.
alternatives_considered: stage of the wiki maintenance workflow (P5)

statement: A day's digest, once written, is never silently regenerated on a later run; the operator must explicitly delete the existing page to force resynthesis, unless running in dry-run mode.
trigger: a digest is requested for a date that already has a written page
outcome: a digest is idempotent by default: re-running the job never clobbers an existing day's synthesized page
rationale: An idempotency rule attached to the digest checkpoint's entry condition, not an independent checkpoint.

statement: The synthesis prompt is built to be driven entirely by an externally-authored schema document (SCHEMA.md), which is treated as the authoritative instructions the model must follow, rather than the digest format being hardcoded into the script.
trigger: a digest is being synthesized
outcome: the digest's exact structure and rules can be changed by editing one schema document, without touching this script
notes: Direct parallel to proposal §4.4 'Procedure remains data': the digest's authoring rules live in a data file the actor reads, not in code.
rationale: SCHEMA.md is externally-authored shared context consumed by this actor stage, matching §6.6's shared-context test.

statement: A digest page notes candidate new entity/decision/feature pages inside a specially fenced block at the end of its body, distinct from the digest content itself, so a later automated pass can capture them for follow-up without needing to re-parse free-form prose.
trigger: synthesis identifies material that deserves its own durable page beyond the daily digest
outcome: candidates for new durable knowledge pages are captured in a machine-recognizable location rather than being lost in free prose
rationale: A structural convention (a specially fenced block) consumed by a separate, later automated pass — matches §6.6.

statement: Evaluating whether a waiting worker's durable wake condition is satisfied recognizes a fixed set of condition kinds — a timestamp, a GitHub check, a sibling fleet task's completion, a tracked-work task's completion, a deployment (unsupported today), or an explicit human response (never auto-evaluable) — and every kind not recognized is treated as needing human input rather than silently ignored.
trigger: a waiting worker's condition is due for evaluation
